summary: syspo exfiltrates clipboard/screen/window text and silently drops Python runtime to bootstrap payload
details: syspo self-describes as a 'System binary configuration tool' but its actual behavior is broad user-activity harvesting. On require()/npm start, index.js executes at top level and, if Python is missing, silently downloads the Python 3.12 Windows installer from python.org to %TEMP% and runs it with /quiet flags (comments describe this as a 'Ghost Install'), then pip-installs supporting packages and spawns pointer.py. pointer.py creates a hidden overlay (empty window titles, overrideredirect, transparent color, stealth hotkeys including a 'panic_exit') and continuously captures clipboard contents via pyperclip, screenshots via mss/ImageGrab, and text scraped from arbitrary application windows via UI Automation (auto.WalkControl(main_window, maxDepth=14)), POSTing the captured data to the hardcoded endpoint https://new-pointer.vercel.app/api. The destination is not caller-configurable. A bundled start_tool.vbs uses ShellExecute with 'runas' and window state 0 to launch the payload silently with administrator elevation. The mismatch between the advertised purpose and the stealth-overlay + hardcoded-exfil-endpoint behavior is a cover story.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
